legal_position: The ICC has no independent police force and depends on state cooperation.
political_effect: Warrants may remain unenforced when suspects retain power or protection.
practice_note: Track arrest feasibility separately from legal validity.

legal_position: Investigations require witness, documentary, digital, forensic, and state cooperation.
political_effect: Active conflicts and hostile governments obstruct evidence collection.
practice_note: Assess chain of custody, witness security, and digital verification.

legal_position: The Council can refer situations but politics affects referral and follow-through.
political_effect: Veto dynamics and uneven enforcement fuel selectivity critiques.
practice_note: Distinguish referral jurisdiction from enforcement commitment.

legal_position: Jurisdiction may still arise through territorial state acceptance or Council referral.
political_effect: Major powers often contest jurisdiction affecting their nationals or allies.
practice_note: Avoid assuming non-party status fully blocks jurisdiction.

legal_position: Legal procedures operate within unequal geopolitical conditions.
political_effect: Regional imbalance, resource limits, and cooperation gaps shape perception.
practice_note: Discuss selectivity without treating it as a complete answer to legality.
